items.risk: Large desalination-project delivery timing creates pronounced quarter-to-quarter revenue volatility, and the CO2 business wind-down demonstrates technology-adjacency execution risk.
High gross margin can coexist with weak shipment timing and does not by itself prove durable growth.
Megaproject concentration and timing can decouple durable freshwater demand from near-term ERII revenue realization.
Adjacent-market success is not implied by core desalination competence; the CO2 retail wind-down is an observed failure analog for causal overextension.
Revenue concentration in large desalination projects can make backlog/TAM narratives misleading if conversion timing and customer awards are not source-addressed.
Confidence inflation is possible if high gross margin is treated as evidence that the volume decline is immaterial.
Substitution and competitive-response risk remain insufficiently quantified in current lineage.
